hypothesis: HYPE breakout-onset entries whose completed five-minute breakout direction agrees with the completed-hour structural direction may outperform entries where those directions oppose after live costs.
decision: Do not add a five-minute direction-agreement gate and do not replace the completed-hour structural entry side. Under the active soft-eight-to-hard-twenty-four-hour exit contract, every development arm remained negative and aligned-only was worse per trade than control or opposed-only. The already-opened final block favored opposed-only, but that result is post-hoc and regime-unstable. Preserve the current live contract and prospectively attribute the resolved current aligned short before reconsidering entry direction.
falsifier: Update this decision if a predeclared prospective sample of exact breakout-side relations shows aligned entries outperforming opposed entries after fees, funding, and slippage, and a causal unopened venue block using the same active lifecycle contract also improves mean return per trade and profit factor without materially worse drawdown.
limitations: The alignment cohorts were defined after inspecting a live direction conflict.
The final sixty-day block had already been opened and is descriptive rather than untouched holdout evidence.
Different retained signals change subsequent position occupancy, so cumulative return sums are not directly comparable across arms.
The offline replay uses one-minute bars and fixed slippage and does not prove live IOC fills.
Only one closed live HYPE lifecycle has exact breakout-side relation coverage; the current aligned lifecycle remains open.
Neither control nor either direction cohort produced a positive development profit factor, so this evidence does not establish a standalone entry edge.
